title: Token-phase & architecture adaptive kernel optimizer for prefill/decode workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Current runtime kernel selection is coarse-grained (static buckets by seqlen and arch) and occasionally selects suboptimal kernels for mixed prefill/decode traffic. This causes latency spikes during short prefill bursts and cost inefficiencies for long decode sessions. We need an adaptive kernel optimizer that is aware of the request token-phase (prefill vs decode), architecture fingerprint, and seqlen distribution to pick or blend kernels online with safe fallbacks.
proposal: Introduce a two-layer autotuner: 1) a lightweight request fingerprint computed at routing time (architecture ID, GPU memory/SM count, median and 95th percentile seqlen estimate for request/session, token_phase tag), hashed to a candidate kernel set; 2) a low-cost cost-latency estimator (microbench-based lookups + small regressor) that ranks candidates under the current occupancy and batch size, with a conservative safety margin. The tuner will run warm-start using nightly microbenchmark snapshots, then perform controlled online probes with strict sampling budgets and SLO-aware rollback. Key features: token-phase aware candidate prioritization (different kernels for prefill heavy vs decode-heavy), occupancy-aware scoring, fallback to conservative kernel if latency risk > threshold, and automatic bake-in of proven candidates to kernel cache. We'll instrument telemetry for per-kernel p50/p95/p99, overflow rejections, and regression alerts. Rollout behind runtime feature flag with canary on dedicated cluster first.
tasks: Design fingerprint schema and hash table layout
Build microbench harness for arch x seqlen x kernel combos and pipeline nightly snapshots
Implement runtime probe agent that performs cheap sampling probes with token_phase context
Train/plug small latency-cost estimator (lightweight regression) using microbench outputs
Add safety controller: sampling budget, SLO thresholds, rollback logic
Expose kernel decision telemetry in Console (per-route kernel choices, latency/cost)
Create canary rollout plan and e2e tests
Write design doc and API contract for kernel hints and metadata
acceptance_criteria: Automated microbench produces nightly snapshot artefact and uploader to artifacts service
Runtime can compute fingerprint and produce candidate ranked list within 250us per request routing decision
Canary fleet shows 10% or better reduction in median token cost on mixed workloads without increasing p99 latency beyond SLO (measured across canary window)
Online probe safety controls successfully rollback within 1 minute if p99 increases by >15%
Console telemetry surfaces per-kernel p95/p99 and choice frequency; team can query history for last 30d
